title: [DECISION] Heap allocation of ikm_buf matches inbuf pattern (not stack)
description: include/uapi/crypto2dev_ioctl.h lines 870-892 and src/cdev/crypto2dev_fd.c lines 1785-1789: When ikm_fd != -1, ikm_buf is allocated on the heap (kmalloc) to hold the extracted key material, not embedded in the ioctl struct or on the stack. This matches the existing inbuf pattern (write-before-ioctl for KEY_IMPORT). The allocation is sized exactly to the IKM length (via CRYPTO2DEV_KDF_OKM_MAXLEN as the temp buffer), not a worst-case constant. This prevents stack overflow when extracting large key material. The comment in the header (lines 864-892) explains the rationale: post-quantum keys exceed 4KB, and embedding them in a struct would land on the kernel stack, violating the ~1KB guideline. Using heap allocation for ikm_buf preserves this discipline: only CRYPTO2DEV_KDF_OKM_MAXLEN bytes are allocated (64 bytes), not a worst-case 8KB, even when the extracted key is smaller.
